text:
Re: Brendan Oduya, 36

Brendan was playing netball 4 days ago when he pushed off and felt a sharp blow to the back of his right ankle; he turned around expecting someone had hit him. He can walk flat-footed but cannot rise onto his toes on that side. On examination there is a soft dip about 4 cm above the heel, and squeezing the calf produces no foot movement. No imaging yet. Otherwise fit, no medications. Currently in a moon boot from the pharmacy.

Dr Hannah Teo
note: Classic acute complete Achilles rupture (palpable gap, positive Thompson test) at 4 days; the operative vs functional-bracing decision is time-critical. Hard because it is described in lay terms and never named as a rupture.

text:
Dear Orthopaedic Team,

Re: Stuart McKellar, 44, carpenter

Six days ago Stuart was lifting a sheet of plywood when he felt a pop in the front of his right elbow. He has bruising over the proximal forearm, the biceps muscle belly has retracted up the arm, and the hook test is negative. Supination is weak and painful. Ultrasound yesterday: complete distal biceps tendon rupture with 5 cm retraction. Right-hand dominant, keen to return to work.

Meds: nil.

Regards,
Dr Priya Raman
note: Acute complete distal biceps rupture in a manual worker; repair is best within 2-3 weeks before retraction makes it difficult.

text:
Re: Kirsty Hallam, 38

Kirsty was thrown from her horse 12 days ago and landed on her outstretched left arm. X-ray showed no fracture or dislocation. Since then she has been unable to lift the arm above shoulder height, with marked weakness of abduction and external rotation, although passive range is nearly full. Ultrasound: full-thickness tears of supraspinatus and infraspinatus, 3.5 cm, retracted to the level of the humeral head. She runs a riding school and is otherwise well.

Dr Marcus Lindqvist
note: Acute traumatic large full-thickness cuff tear in a young active patient; early repair (ideally within weeks) gives the best outcome.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Geoffrey Pham, 58, missed a step at home 4 days ago and his left knee buckled. He now cannot straight-leg raise or walk without the knee giving way, and there is a palpable defect just above the patella with a large effusion. X-ray: low-lying patella, no fracture. Background type 2 diabetes on metformin, eGFR 70. He works as a courier.

I have given him a knee immobiliser and crutches.

Thanks,
Dr Olivia Sandhu
note: Acute quadriceps tendon rupture with loss of extensor mechanism needs early surgical repair.

text:
Re: Jarrah Collins, 24

Jarrah twisted his right knee playing Aussie rules a week ago. The next morning he could not straighten it, and it has stayed stuck about 25 degrees short of full extension, with medial joint line tenderness and a moderate effusion. He is walking on crutches. MRI on Friday: displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus flipped into the intercondylar notch, ACL intact.

Meds: ibuprofen prn.

Dr Fiona Grech
note: Locked knee from a displaced bucket-handle meniscal tear in a young patient; early arthroscopic repair improves the chance of saving the meniscus.

text:
Re: Maddison Kerr, 19

Maddison fell onto her outstretched right hand at a roller-skating party 10 days ago. ED X-rays of the wrist were reported as normal and she was told it was a sprain. She still has pain on gripping and writing, and today she is clearly tender in the anatomical snuffbox and over the scaphoid tubercle, with pain on thumb telescoping. She has not been immobilised. She is a university student and right-handed.

Dr Callum Yeo
note: Clinically suspected scaphoid fracture despite normal initial X-ray, persisting at 10 days and not immobilised; needs prompt immobilisation and CT/MRI to avoid non-union. Hard because the letter frames it as a sprain with normal X-rays.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Ravi Krishnan, 33

Ravi rolled his left ankle playing futsal 3 weeks ago and was told at a clinic that it was a bad sprain; no X-ray was done then. He still cannot bear weight without crutches and the swelling has not settled. X-ray this week: displaced fracture of the distal fibula at the level of the syndesmosis with widening of the medial clear space. Non-smoker, no medical history.

Kind regards,
Dr Amelia Fox
note: Unstable displaced ankle fracture (Weber B with medial clear space widening) referred late; fixation should not be delayed further.

text:
Re: Theresa Bianchi, 45

Plaster check, please. Theresa had a closed reduction of a left distal radius fracture at our local hospital 11 days ago after a fall at netball, and was sent home in a backslab. The check X-ray I arranged today shows the fracture has slipped: dorsal angulation now 25 degrees and about 4 mm of radial shortening. She has some tingling in the thumb and index finger but good capillary refill. She is a dental nurse, left-handed.

Dr Brian Kowalczyk
note: Loss of reduction of a distal radius fracture at 11 days in a working-age patient, with median nerve symptoms; the window for surgical fixation before malunion is short. Hard because it is framed as a routine plaster check.

text:
Re: Anthony Russo, 52, fencing contractor

Anthony has known for 2 years about a small supraspinatus tear in his right shoulder, which settled with physiotherapy; he had been working without restriction. Nine days ago he slipped on a wet ramp and fell onto the shoulder. Since then he cannot actively lift the arm at all. Repeat ultrasound: the tear has extended to a full-thickness tear of supraspinatus and infraspinatus, 4 cm, with retraction. Passive movement is preserved.

Dr Leanne Moss
note: Acute traumatic extension of a small chronic cuff tear in an active 52-year-old with new pseudoparalysis; early repair is time-critical. Hard because the old known tear could make it read as chronic degenerative disease.

text:
Dear Cardiologist,

Re: Pauline Gregory, 62

Pauline presented 3 weeks ago with palpitations and was found to be in atrial fibrillation, rate 130. I started metoprolol and apixaban. Her rate is now around 105 but she is breathless walking up one flight of stairs, sleeps on three pillows and has new ankle oedema. Echo last week: LVEF 35%, no significant valve disease; no previous echo. Her BP is 118/76. She was fully active before this.

Dr Nikhil Bose
note: New AF with heart failure symptoms and reduced EF, possibly tachycardia-mediated; an early rhythm-control decision (cardioversion/ablation) affects recovery of LV function.

text:
Re: Gemma Thorpe, 41

Gemma has a mole on her left calf that her partner says has changed over the past 3 months. It is now 8 mm, asymmetric, with uneven brown and black colour and an irregular notched border; a small pink area has appeared at one edge. Dermoscopy shows an atypical pigment network and blue-white structures. She has fair skin and many naevi, and her mother had a melanoma. No palpable lymph nodes.

Dr Sophie Tran
note: Changing pigmented lesion with features suspicious of melanoma; needs urgent excision.

text:
Re: Lachlan Doherty, 29

Lachlan has ulcerative colitis known to your unit. He flared 3 weeks ago and I started prednisolone 40 mg daily 15 days ago, on top of mesalazine. He is no better: 6 to 7 bloody stools a day, waking at night, urgency. Afebrile, pulse 90. Bloods: CRP 28, Hb 118 (was 139), albumin 33. Stool cultures and C. difficile negative. I have told him to go to ED if he worsens.

Dr Ingrid Paulsen
note: Moderate-to-severe UC flare not responding to 2 weeks of oral steroids; escalation (biologic/admission) is a time-critical decision even though he is not yet acutely unstable.

text:
Re: Barbara Nolan, 68

Barbara has had right shoulder pain for 8 months, worse at night and with reaching overhead, with no injury. She has had 12 weeks of physiotherapy and a subacromial steroid injection, which helped for 6 weeks. She can still lift the arm fully, with a painful arc. Ultrasound: partial-thickness bursal-side tear of supraspinatus with tendinosis and subacromial bursitis. Her sleep is disrupted most nights.

Meds: amlodipine, paracetamol.

Dr Craig Wallis
note: Degenerative partial-thickness cuff tear in an older patient with failed conservative care and sleep disturbance; ongoing pain but no risk of rapid deterioration.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Simon Ferris, 51, postal worker

Simon has 9 months of right insertional Achilles pain. He walks most of the day on his round and is now struggling to finish shifts. He has done 12 weeks of loading exercises with a physio, heel lifts and shockwave therapy without much change. There is a tender thickened insertion with a prominent posterior heel. Ultrasound: insertional tendinopathy with calcification, no tear. Calf squeeze normal.

Regards,
Dr Mei Ling Ong
note: Chronic insertional Achilles tendinopathy without tear, failing conservative care and affecting work; disability without risk of rapid deterioration.

text:
Re: Harold Jensen, 74

Harold felt a snap in his left heel when stepping off a kerb about 9 months ago but did not mention it until his recent check-up. He walks independently, does lawn bowls twice a week and has no pain. He cannot do a single-leg heel raise on the left and his calf is smaller. Ultrasound: old Achilles rupture with the gap filled by scar tissue, tendon lengthened. He wanted to know whether anything should be done.

Dr Penelope Hart
note: Old untreated Achilles rupture that has healed functionally in an older low-demand patient; no time-critical decision remains. Hard because the word rupture and a positive history could prompt urgent.

text:
Re: Kieran Walsh, 26

Kieran had an undisplaced scaphoid waist fracture in March, treated in a cast for 8 weeks by the fracture clinic, who discharged him. CT in June showed union. He has mild stiffness in wrist extension and some aching after a long day at the computer. He would like an opinion on whether it is safe to return to rugby union this season, and whether he needs any further imaging.

Dr Josephine Lau
note: Healed scaphoid fracture with mild stiffness and a return-to-sport question. Hard because 'scaphoid fracture' is a high-risk phrase.

text:
Re: Linda Moretti, 49

Linda has 3 months of medial left knee pain after twisting it while gardening. It aches after long walks and on stairs. She has never had locking or giving way, has full extension and flexion, and the effusion has settled. MRI: horizontal degenerative tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with early medial compartment chondral thinning. She manages with paracetamol and is doing a strengthening program.

Dr Ahmed Siddiqui
note: Stable degenerative meniscal tear without mechanical symptoms in a middle-aged patient; first-line care is non-operative.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Daryl Simmons, 45, plumber

Six months of lateral right elbow pain, worse with gripping tools and turning taps. He is still working but takes ibuprofen most days. He has had two steroid injections, a counterforce brace and physiotherapy. Tender over the lateral epicondyle, pain on resisted wrist extension. Full elbow range, no neurological symptoms. He has asked about other options.

Dr Rosalind Achebe
note: Lateral epicondylalgia (tennis elbow); self-limiting, working with modification.

text:
Re: Carol Fitzgerald, 55

Carol has had heel pain under the right foot for 10 months, worst with her first steps in the morning and after sitting. She has tried calf stretches, a night splint, off-the-shelf orthotics and weight loss of 4 kg. Tender at the medial calcaneal tubercle. X-ray: small plantar heel spur. She works in a bakery and is on her feet all day but managing.

Dr Tobias Wren
note: Chronic plantar fasciitis; managing, no deterioration risk.

text:
Dear Orthopaedics,

Re: Neville Archer, 61

Three weeks ago Neville felt his biceps 'snap' while starting a lawnmower, with a loud pop and a large bruise down the arm. There is now an obvious bulge low in the right upper arm. The pain has settled, and elbow flexion and supination strength are near normal. Ultrasound: rupture of the long head of biceps at the shoulder; the distal tendon is intact. He is retired and plays golf.

Dr Wendy Cartwright
note: Proximal long-head biceps rupture in an older patient; usually managed non-operatively, no time-critical decision. Hard because the dramatic 'snap' and the word rupture mimic a distal biceps rupture.

text:
Re: Patrick Oyelaran, 38

Patrick inverted his right foot stepping off a ladder 5 weeks ago. X-ray showed an undisplaced avulsion fracture at the base of the fifth metatarsal. He has been in a walking boot and the pain is settling; repeat X-ray this week shows early healing with no displacement. He is walking short distances without the boot. He has asked whether he needs to see a specialist before returning to work.

Dr Ellen Murray
note: Stable, healing fifth metatarsal base avulsion fracture.

text:
Re: Gordon Pike, 57

Gordon has a massive right rotator cuff tear first diagnosed on ultrasound 3 years ago. He describes the shoulder as 'wrecked': constant aching, worse at night, and he can no longer lift a kettle to the top shelf. X-ray now shows superior migration of the humeral head with early glenohumeral arthritis. He has had physio and two injections with only short benefit. No recent injury. Retired forklift driver.

Dr Charlotte Ng
note: Chronic massive cuff tear progressing to cuff tear arthropathy, with pain and loss of function but no acute event; an operation such as reverse arthroplasty can be planned. Hard because 'massive tear' and the dramatic language sound acute.

text:
Re: Jasmine Kovacs, 31

Jasmine ruptured her left ACL skiing 8 months ago (MRI-confirmed). She completed 5 months of physiotherapy. The knee is fine for daily life and work, but it has given way three times playing netball, the last time 6 weeks ago, with a small effusion that settled. No locking, full range. She would like to discuss reconstruction so she can return to netball.

Meds: nil.

Dr Adrian Fuller
note: Chronic ACL deficiency with sport-related instability after failed rehabilitation; reconstruction is elective. Hard because the word rupture and episodes of giving way could prompt urgent.

text:
Re: Tyler Brooks, 22

Tyler plays representative volleyball and has 6 months of pain at the lower pole of his left kneecap, worse with jumping and after training. He is training at reduced load. Tender at the inferior patellar pole, full range, no effusion. Ultrasound: proximal patellar tendinopathy with neovascularity, no tear. He has done 8 weeks of isometric and heavy slow loading with his club physio.

Dr Isabelle Moreau
note: Patellar tendinopathy without tear; minimal dysfunction outside sport.

text:
Re: Natalie Sorensen, 34

Natalie has had migraine without aura since her teens. Over the past year she has averaged 6 migraine days a month, with good response to sumatriptan. Neurological exam normal. Propranolol caused fatigue and she stopped it; she is now on amitriptyline 10 mg with partial benefit. She is not using analgesics more than 8 days a month. She would like to discuss other preventive options.

Dr Hugh Patterson
note: Episodic migraine with normal exam needing preventive advice.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Darren Whitlock, 47

Darren has asthma that has been poorly controlled for the past 9 months despite budesonide/formoterol 400/12 two puffs twice daily with good technique and adherence. He has needed two courses of prednisolone this year and wakes with wheeze two or three nights a week. Spirometry: FEV1 68% predicted with 18% reversibility. Blood eosinophils 0.6. Non-smoker. No ED visits.

Kind regards,
Dr Ruth Abernethy
note: Uncontrolled asthma on high-dose ICS/LABA with eosinophilia, possibly suitable for a biologic; significant symptoms but not unstable.

text:
Re: Kenneth Lowry, 66

Kenneth's bowel screening FOBT was positive last month. He has also noticed his bowel motions have been looser and more frequent for about 2 months, with some urgency in the mornings. Bloods: Hb 109 (was 141 a year ago), MCV 76, ferritin 8. No overt bleeding. He has lost about 3 kg without trying. No previous colonoscopy. Meds: perindopril, rosuvastatin.

Dr Abigail Strang
note: Positive FOBT with new iron-deficiency anaemia, change in bowel habit and weight loss; suspected colorectal cancer.

text:
Re: Marcus Delaney, 39

Marcus has chronic plaque psoriasis affecting about 12% of his body surface, including his scalp, elbows, knees and lower back. He has used potent topical steroids and calcipotriol for years with partial control. It itches enough to disturb his sleep and he is self-conscious at work. No joint symptoms. He would like to be assessed for phototherapy or systemic treatment.

Dr Yvonne Chua
note: Moderate psoriasis failing topical treatment; affects quality of life, not at risk of rapid deterioration.

text:
Re: Fiona Gallagher, 44

Fiona has noticed 'skipped beats' for about 6 months, mostly in the evenings, lasting seconds. No syncope, chest pain or breathlessness. She runs 5 km three times a week without symptoms. ECG normal. Holter: sinus rhythm with isolated ventricular ectopics, 1.5% burden, no runs. Echo: structurally normal heart. TSH normal. She drinks 3 coffees a day. She would value reassurance.

Dr Gareth Hollis
note: Benign low-burden ectopy with normal structural work-up; reassurance only.

text:
Re: Olga Petrenko, 58

Olga has had a dry cough for 5 months that started after a viral illness. No haemoptysis, weight loss, fever or breathlessness. Never smoked. CXR and spirometry are normal. She is not on an ACE inhibitor. A 6-week trial of a nasal steroid and 8 weeks of a PPI made no difference. It is mostly a nuisance at work and when talking on the phone.

Dr Luke Harrington
note: Chronic cough with normal CXR and spirometry and no red flags.
